contributions.statement: When an agent mines ticket and chat history to find discussions behind a spec item, query from the concrete tracking ticket rather than the high-level roadmap goal and have a human confirm the top-5 candidates; issue-to-discussion ranking reached P@5 0.62-0.91 versus 0.53-0.73 from goals.
contributions.evidence: §6.3 Table 13 (GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-R1, zero-shot and CoT) and the abstraction-gap explanation in §6.4A. Caveats: 9 Rust cases, one run per configuration, precision only with no recall or ground truth, links validated by the authors (kappa 0.83 on a 10% subset), undocumented candidate pre-filter, no BM25 or embedding baseline.
relative_to: LLM traceability recovery with prompt engineering (TraceLLM, Alturayeif et al. 2026, cited)
2608.00705: requirement-trace retrieval degrades as hop distance grows

contributions.statement: Do not let a small local model (7-9B) draft requirement specs or acceptance criteria from raw user feedback without a per-requirement source check, because its drafts scored 3.0/5 on fidelity and added requirements absent from the input.
contributions.evidence: §5.3 RQ3 Table 8 (average fidelity 3.0, conciseness 2.3) and §5.4B. Caveats: 90 app reviews, rated by the first author alone with no reliability check, no human-written comparison, models from 2023-24.
relative_to: LLM hallucination in generated requirements and specifications (known before 2026)
Mallya et al., REFSQ 2026 (the same authors' earlier publication of Study I)

reason: Study I is a ranking of dated small models and prompts on public app-review datasets, already published, and transfers nothing the team can act on. Study II's only actionable nuance is that ticket-level queries trace to discussions better than goal-level ones. It rests on nine single-run cases with no recall and no baseline, so it remains a hypothesis to test on the team's own ticket and chat history.
